long_biography.plain_text:
After studying assisted-housing models in Scandinavia, Miha Jarc adapted the concept for Slovenian buyers who wanted independent homes rather than institutional care. Mijaks combined accessible design with optional support services, creating owner-occupied apartments for older residents who could still live largely independently.

That concept became a sustained specialism within Jarc's wider residential-development business. Early work in Ljubljana included a land exchange under which Mijaks delivered assisted apartments to the municipal housing fund, linking private development with public housing provision. The group later extended the model to other Slovenian locations while continuing conventional residential projects. Jarc remains its owner and director, overseeing the business's investment and development work.
